specGaps: SG-1 (§3.7.2's signature is self-defeating) — VERIFIED REAL: run.counters lives inside run.json (core/types.ts:205), so hashing raw run.json makes every re-prompt look like progress and futileRePrompts can never reach 3. RESOLUTION: hash a canonical projection that EXCLUDES run.counters, serialized with sorted keys — {run.state, run.classification.kind, run.planReviewRounds, items sorted by id as {id, state, blockedReason (null when unblocked), deferredReason (null when undeferred)}, questions sorted by id as {id, answered: boolean}}. Deliberately NARROW: every extra field is another way for a wedged run to look like it moved, and the whole point of the counter is to end a run that is not moving. Row 10.1-futile-signature-excludes-counters pins the counters-only case; row 10.1-signature-change-resets pins the three change classes.

SG-2 (idling with no recommendation) — §3.7.1 re-prompts while 'actionable work exists', but core/gates-phase.ts:396 shows a reachable non-terminal EXECUTING verdict with recommended:null (blocked item + a dependent that is neither schedulable nor settled). The plan's 10.1 bullet only tests the recommended case. RESOLUTION: re-prompt ONLY when recommended !== null. A null-recommendation non-terminal idle journals continuation/idle carrying legalTools' authoritative `why`, prompts nothing, and leaves counters untouched — so it neither burns tokens nor counts as futile. The run's exit in that shape is conductor_answer by the human (the gate keeps it legal), which is exactly what §2.9 intends by leaving 'blocked' to the report tool.

SG-3 (where the debounce state lives) — §3.7.4's 2s window and 'one in flight' have no home in the §2.3 schema, and adding one would be a schema change. RESOLUTION: both are IN-MEMORY on the engine instance (one instance per plugin process, the same process that holds the workspace lock). The durable half is counters.idleRePrompts / futileRePrompts and the last signature, which is derived from persisted state and so survives a restart; a process restart may re-prompt once inside the 2s window, which is harmless and strictly better than persisting a timestamp the schema has no field for.

SG-4 (archival timing and scope) — C-029(a) says 'wire archival where the run lifecycle is managed' and §3.2:1081 says a question run is archived, but nothing says WHEN, nor whether stop-terminal and REPORTED runs are archived too. RESOLUTION: the engine archives ANY terminal run it observes at idle, in the SAME pass, AFTER any stop-report it owes and AFTER worktree cleanup. archiveRun only clears the pointer (state.ts:553) so it is idempotent and safe if 9.5b's report handler ever archives first. CONSEQUENCE the tests encode: after archival store.currentRun() is null, so the next idle finds no live run and does nothing — which is why cleanup cannot be deferred to a later pass.

SG-5 (how a rejected sub-session ask becomes NEEDS_CONTEXT) — §3.5(b) says 'the fan-out engine converts the blocked state into NEEDS_CONTEXT or a surfaced question', but NEEDS_CONTEXT is a field of the sub-session's own structured reply (core/types.ts:423) and adapter/fanout.ts has no permission awareness and no channel for a mid-session event (FanoutResult:66 is {sessionID, value, error, timings}). Editing the committed 9.4a/9.4c consuming handlers to read a new channel is outside this task's bullet. RESOLUTION: handlePermissionAsked returns AND records a conversion {sessionID, itemId, status:'NEEDS_CONTEXT', neededContext} reusing the §2.10 ImplementerStatus vocabulary (no new status, no schema change), and the ENGINE surfaces it to the orchestrator in its next re-prompt text — the one channel 10.1 owns end to end. Queue is in-memory, drained on surface, so a second idle does not repeat it. Recorded as a deviation from the plan's 'the fan-out engine converts': the conversion is produced by the ask-gate and delivered by the continuation engine, which is the same information reaching the same reader.

SG-6 (where the C-029(b) guard lives) — the binding says 'the 10.1 ask-gate', but conductor_decide arrives as a TOOL CALL, never as a permission ask, and continuation.ts must import the report writer, waveVerdict and handlerRunDir FROM adapter/tools.ts, so a tools.ts -> continuation.ts import would close a cycle. RESOLUTION: the guard is a second legality check INSIDE handleDecide (adapter/tools.ts:740), immediately beside requireTwoOptions at :757, calling the pure core/decide.ts isHumanTerritory — 'the ask-gate' in the binding names the RULE, not the file. The module edge stays one-way: continuation.ts -> tools.ts, never back.

SG-7 (the stop-report writer's name) — see dependsOnUnbuilt. The rows are written against 'the ONE §2.9 stop-report writer in its stop mode'. If 9.5c's export is named differently, only the assertion text's spelling changes; the requirement — one writer, zero re-implementations in continuation.ts, and the stale-red registration happening through it — is what the rows enforce.

SG-8 (what makes an inline claim ACTIVE) — §3.6 grants edit permission 'scoped to that item's fileScope until the item leaves its current state', but the persisted record is only {reason, decisionId} (core/types.ts:249, sharing reasonDecisionOrNullSchema with `deferred` at :498): it stores neither a scope nor the state it was claimed in. RESOLUTION for 10.1: active means `item.inlineClaim !== null && item.state !== 'PUBLISHED'`, and the scope is that item's queue.json fileScope — one derivation, exported, used by BOTH the ask reply and the tool.execute.before seam. RESIDUAL, recorded not papered over: the mid-FSM half of §3.6's expiry ('leaves its CURRENT state') is not computable from committed state and is NOT implemented here; closing it needs either a claimedInState field on the Item schema (a §2.5 schema change ⇒ STOP-AND-PARK) or a clear-on-transition sweep across every handler that advances an item (six call sites at tools.ts:2469/3410/3849/3911/4181, outside this bullet). Raised for the Phase 10 review; 15.1 HONEST-LIMITS.md is the sink if it stays open. The conservative half IS implemented: a claim on a PUBLISHED item covers nothing.

SG-9 (the orchestrator has no tree) — adapter/chat-message.ts:75 registers {role:'orchestrator'} with no `tree`, and both decideEdit consumers read `entry.tree ?? ''`, which mangles absolute paths (gates-edit.ts:118: '/repo/src/a.ts' -> 'repo/src/a.ts'). RESOLUTION: ONE exported helper resolves the session tree as `entry.tree ?? <workspace root>` and BOTH seams use it. chat-message.ts is NOT edited (it would overwrite any tree the plugin wrote on the next user prompt, so patching the registry entry would be a race); the fallback is idempotent under that overwrite.

SG-10 (the ask payload's file path is not wire-pinned) — wire-notes.md:110 states patterns/metadata were never asserted, so which field carries the edit's file path is UNVERIFIED. RESOLUTION: extract in order — metadata.filePath, then metadata.path, then a single concrete (wildcard-free) entry of patterns — and FAIL CLOSED: an orchestrator edit ask whose path cannot be extracted is REJECTED and journaled, never allowed. This is safe under G5 (rejecting an orchestrator edit is the G8 default the run already lives with, not a request the direct path would have served) and it degrades to 'inline claim does not work' rather than 'the orchestrator can edit anything'. Task 13.2's live smoke is where the real payload gets pinned into wire-notes.md; row 10.1-ask-path-unextractable-reject is the guard until then.

SG-11 (the plugin has no store) — plugin/index.ts holds only a Map registry and a stderr journal, and its `runId` is input.project.id (:72), which is not a conductor runId. The event hook needs run state (for the engine) and item state (for the claim scope). RESOLUTION: the plugin opens the workspace ONCE (adapter/state.ts openWorkspace) and injects that single store into the engine, the ask-gate and the tool.execute.before wiring — one writer per process (G6), and openWorkspace's own readOnly degradation (state.ts:234) handles the case where another process holds the lock. The correlation runId comes from store.currentRun()?.runId, never from project.id.

SG-12 (the other crash/partial-write parks) — CORRECTIONS parks five more classes at 10.1: C-030 E10 (a crash inside handleDecompose/handlePlan's persist phase leaves orphaned decisions.jsonl rows and orphaned PENDING item files absent from queue.json) and C-031 (a) E4 half-applied plan-review cap, (b) E7 revision counter saved after the plan it counts, (c) E8 a surviving major naming a missing item file wedges the run at PLANNED, (d) F4 partially advanced run across lens aborts, (e) F5 duplicate decision rows per revision round. RESOLUTION: NOT implemented here, and NOT silently dropped. Each is a write-ORDERING defect inside a specific committed handler, repairable only by giving that handler an idempotent resume key; a continuation engine cannot reconstruct the intent of a half-finished decompose from the outside, and attempting it would invent state. The ONE park with a repair that needs no new vocabulary — C-032 E7's question/setBlocked window, where both writes are fully determined and the second is idempotent — IS implemented (rows 10.1-binding-orphan-question-reconcile / -question-reuse-no-duplicate). The remaining five are re-parked to Task 15.1 HONEST-LIMITS.md with this reasoning, and flagged for the orchestrator at the Phase 10 review; the Phase 9 MILESTONE gate is NOT a valid sink for them because it runs before this task.

SG-13 (who owns the anomaly append) — nothing writes anomalies.jsonl at HEAD, adapter/state.ts appendLedgerLineRaw is reserved to evidence.ts by its own contract (state.ts:169-172, evidence.ts:12), and 9.5c needs the same appender for kind:'override'. RESOLUTION: ONE `appendAnomaly(runDir, record)` in adapter/tools.ts beside appendDecision (:464) — validate('AnomalyRecord', record) then append one line. 10.1 reuses 9.5c's if it landed first and creates it there if not; continuation.ts never defines its own.

SG-14 (two different 're-prompts') — the 9.2/9.3 handlers each grant ONE bounded re-prompt to a sub-session inside a single tool call (C-030's documented deviation F5). That is a fan-out retry and has nothing to do with §3.7's idle re-prompt of the ORCHESTRATOR. They share a word, not a counter: counters.idleRePrompts is touched only by the continuation engine, and no handler's internal round may increment it.

assertions.text: a session.idle event whose sessionID resolves to a registry entry with role !== 'orchestrator' (e.g. 'implementer'), or to NO registry entry at all, produces ZERO client.session.prompt calls and ZERO writes: run.json is byte-identical afterwards (counters unchanged) and no journal record under the `continuation` component is emitted. §3.7.1's engine is the ORCHESTRATOR's; a sub-session going idle is the fan-out engine's business

an orchestrator session.idle while store.currentRun() is null — no run yet, or the pointer already cleared by a previous archival pass — produces zero prompts, zero writes and no throw; the handler returns normally. This is the state every archived run leaves behind (state.ts:553 clears the pointer), so it must be a quiet no-op rather than an error path

an orchestrator session.idle on a NON-TERMINAL run whose verdict carries a non-null recommendation produces EXACTLY ONE client.session.prompt call, addressed to the orchestrator's own sessionID, whose composed text (fake-sdk PromptRecord.text) contains the recommended tool name and — when the recommendation carries args.itemId — that item id; run.counters.idleRePrompts increases by exactly 1 and is read back from the PERSISTED run.json (through store.saveRun's schema validation); one journal record continuation/reprompt is emitted carrying the tool name. Zero sub-sessions are created (fake-sdk creates is empty): a re-prompt is a message, not a dispatch

the named action is READ from core/gates-phase.ts legalTools via adapter/tools.ts waveVerdict, never re-derived: on two fixtures that differ only in item position (one with I1 at PENDING/behavioral ⇒ conductor_submit_test{I1}; one with I1 at VALIDATED ⇒ conductor_item_review{I1}) the prompt text names the tool legalTools returns for that fixture, and in NEITHER case does the text name a tool absent from verdict.legal. Asserted by computing legalTools on the same fixture inside the test and comparing — the same single-source rule core/gates-phase.ts:155-162 already states for the injection and the continuation engine

SG-2: an orchestrator idle on a non-terminal EXECUTING run whose verdict has recommended === null (fixture: I1 BLOCKED, I2 dependsOn I1 — I2 is unschedulable and unsettled, so the wave is empty and conductor_report is not legal, core/gates-phase.ts:396) produces ZERO prompts, leaves counters.idleRePrompts AND counters.futileRePrompts unchanged, and emits exactly one journal record continuation/idle whose data carries legalTools' authoritative `why` string verbatim. The engine never invents a next step the gate did not offer, and a run it cannot advance is not counted as a futile re-prompt

§3.7.4 debounce, with the clock INJECTED so the test never sleeps: after a re-prompt at t0, an idle at t0+1999ms produces zero additional prompt calls and leaves counters.idleRePrompts unchanged; an idle at t0+2000ms produces one. The window is measured from the last re-prompt, not from the last idle — a burst of idles inside one window yields exactly one prompt in total

at most ONE re-prompt is in flight: with the fake SDK's responder parking the first prompt (pending), an idle arriving after the debounce window has elapsed but while that prompt is still unsettled produces ZERO additional prompt calls and no counter change; after resolvePending settles it, a later idle re-prompts normally. Debounce and in-flight are INDEPENDENT guards — this row's second idle is outside the 2s window, so passing it cannot be an artifact of the debounce

SG-1: the futility signature is a canonical projection that EXCLUDES run.counters — {run.state, run.classification.kind, run.planReviewRounds, items sorted by id as {id, state, blockedReason, deferredReason}, questions sorted by id as {id, answered}}, serialized with sorted keys. Asserted behaviourally: across three consecutive re-prompt passes in which NOTHING changes except counters.idleRePrompts (which the engine itself increments), counters.futileRePrompts reads 1 then 2 then 3 from the persisted run.json. A signature over raw run.json would hold it at 0 forever, so this row fails against the literal §3.7.2 wording and passes against the projection

ANY state change resets counters.futileRePrompts to 0, asserted independently for three change classes, each starting from a persisted futileRePrompts of 2: (a) an item advances (PENDING -> RED); (b) a disposition appears (an item gains blocked, or an open question becomes answered); (c) the run state advances (PLANNED -> PLAN_REVIEWED). In all three the next idle writes futileRePrompts 0 and still re-prompts; the reset is read back from run.json, not from an in-memory field

the wedge ends loudly and deterministically: on a fixture where nothing ever changes, successive idles (each outside the debounce window) produce EXACTLY THREE prompt calls, and the FOURTH idle produces none — instead the engine consults core/stops.ts shouldTerminate with the persisted counters and records run.stop = {kind:'noop', reasonDisplay naming the futile re-prompt count, tsMs from the injected clock} through store.saveRun. Every subsequent idle produces zero prompts and does not re-record the stop (isTerminal short-circuits it). The threshold is never restated in continuation.ts: FUTILE_RE_PROMPT_LIMIT is private at core/stops.ts:84, and the engine reads no env var — deleting the shouldTerminate call must fail this row

§2.8 write-ahead: the noop path appends a schema-valid AnomalyRecord {ts, kind:'disengage', detail} (core/types.ts:329, validated through validate('AnomalyRecord', …)) to runs/<runId>/anomalies.jsonl, and it appends it BEFORE the stop-report is written — proven by injecting a report writer that throws: the handler still returns without propagating (fail-soft), and after the pass anomalies.jsonl carries the disengage line AND run.json carries stop.kind 'noop'. One journal record continuation/disengage is emitted. A killed process leaves its trace

the noop path writes the §2.9 stop-report by invoking the ONE mode-parameterized report writer (Task 9.5b's writer in Task 9.5c's stop mode — see dependsOnUnbuilt) and contains NO report-writing code of its own: runs/<runId>/report.md exists after the pass with the stop kind in its headline; ZERO §2.6 evidence records of kind 'verify' were appended during the pass (read from evidence.jsonl — a stop-report never re-runs the verify, §2.9); and the abandoned red tests are registered in the §2.11 stale-red registry, read back via store.readStaleRed(), WITHOUT continuation.ts ever naming store.addStaleRed (the registration happens inside the shared helper C-037 ruling 4 mandates)

the engine records ONLY the two stop kinds §2.9 assigns to it. On a fixture where shouldTerminate returns {stop:true, kind:'blocked'} (every item blocked, futileRePrompts 0) the engine writes NO stop at all — run.stop stays null — and instead re-prompts the recommended tool (conductor_report, which the gate legalizes because blocked items are settled); the same holds for a 'surfaced' verdict and for an 'env' verdict from an exhausted override budget. blocked/surfaced/done stay with the report tool and env with the fan-out engine (§2.9:900-905). Only noop (this engine's futility rule) and interrupt (halt) are ever written here

§3.7.3: with the halt file present (store.isHalted() true), an orchestrator idle produces ZERO prompt calls even when the run is non-terminal, has a non-null recommendation, has futileRePrompts 0, and is INSIDE the 2s debounce window — halt outranks every other condition and is checked before the debounce and before the recommendation. The engine records run.stop {kind:'interrupt', reasonDisplay naming the halt file} and writes the stop-report through the same single writer; NO disengage anomaly is written (a human halt is not a §2.8 anomaly — that kind belongs to the noop wedge alone), and one continuation/disengage journal record is emitted

isTerminal runs are NEVER re-prompted, asserted for all FOUR shapes with zero prompt calls and zero counter writes each: state ANSWERED, state REPORTED, state TRIVIAL_DONE, and — the case the plan flags as previously missed — state EXECUTING with a recorded stop. The decision comes from core/stops.ts isTerminal (:74), so the fourth case passes for the same reason the first three do; continuation.ts holds no terminal-state list of its own

C-029(a) BINDING, SG-4: a terminal run observed at idle is ARCHIVED in that same pass via store.archiveRun(runId) — pinned specifically for the ANSWERED run conductor_classify's question path leaves behind (handleClassify is NOT edited by this task): after the pass store.currentRun() === null while runs/<runId>/run.json is still readable on disk with state ANSWERED, so §3.2:1081 'state ANSWERED, run archived' holds end to end. Asserted for a stop-terminal run too (EXECUTING + stop noop), and the call is idempotent — a second idle finds no live run and neither throws nor re-archives

C-037 ruling 6 / the 9.6 binding: on the archival pass, and BEFORE the pointer is cleared, the engine calls adapter/worktrees.ts removeWorktree(workspace, runId, itemId) for every queue item whose persisted item.worktree !== null and for NO other item — asserted against a fixture repo by `git worktree list` naming none of the run's worktrees afterwards and the state-home worktree directories being gone, with an item that never had a worktree contributing no call. archiveRun itself still deletes nothing (the 9.6 pin holds); the removal is 10.1's call, so a run that ends any way — done, noop or interrupt — leaves no orphaned worktree behind

the plugin factory's returned hooks object gains an `event` hook (typeof 'function', alongside the unchanged `tool` map and `tool.execute.before`), and it ROUTES by event.type: a {type:'session.idle', properties:{sessionID}} payload reaches the idle engine (observable: a re-prompt on a fixture that warrants one) and a {type:'permission.asked', properties:{id, sessionID, permission, patterns, metadata}} payload reaches the ask gate (observable: a recorded reply). Every OTHER event type — including 'permission.replied' and 'session.created' — is ignored: no prompt, no reply, no throw. CONDUCTOR_TOOL_NAMES and the §3.4 inventory assertion are untouched by this task

G5 fail-soft: a throw from inside either handler (injected — e.g. a store whose loadRun throws) is CAUGHT by the event hook, journaled once at error level under an existing closed-vocab name, and NOT propagated out of the hook (the returned promise resolves). A conductor bug must not kill the opencode session that would otherwise still work; this is the same fail-soft posture §3.8 takes for a plugin whose init fails

registry-first, mirroring the committed 5.3-registry-first rule: a permission.asked whose sessionID has NO registry entry is REJECTED — exactly one reply with response 'reject' — and journaled gates/deny naming the missing registration, whatever the permission kind. An unregistered session is never granted anything on the strength of the ask alone

§3.5(b): a permission.asked from a session whose registry role is a sub-session role (implementer / test-writer / reviewer / skeptic / planner / mechanical) is REJECTED for EVERY permission kind — including 'question', since §5.3 gives sub-agents question:'ask' precisely so the plugin can see and refuse it. The reply goes through the wire-verified route: exactly one client.postSessionIdPermissionsPermissionId({path:{id: sessionID, permissionID: properties.id}, body:{response:'reject'}}) recorded by the extended fake (NOT the plan's client.permission.reply spelling, wire-notes.md:55-59), journaled gates/deny. A REPEAT delivery of the same permission id sends NO second reply — the bus may re-deliver, and adjudication is once per id

SG-5: the rejection converts to a NEEDS_CONTEXT disposition surfaced to the orchestrator. handlePermissionAsked records {sessionID, itemId (from the registry entry), status:'NEEDS_CONTEXT' (the committed §2.10 ImplementerStatus member, core/types.ts:102-108 — no new status invented), neededContext naming the denied permission and its patterns}, and the ENGINE's next orchestrator re-prompt text contains the item id and that neededContext string (asserted on the fake's PromptRecord.text). It is surfaced EXACTLY ONCE: a second idle re-prompts without repeating it. The item's own FSM state and blocked disposition are unchanged by the conversion — supplying context is the orchestrator's move, not a state write

§3.6: an ORCHESTRATOR edit ask for an ABSOLUTE path under the workspace root, while the item carrying the path in its queue fileScope has a non-null item.inlineClaim, is replied ALLOW with response 'once' (the only affirmative response wire-verified, wire-notes.md:34). Coverage is decided by core/gates-edit.ts decideEdit (:149) called with sessionRole 'orchestrator', inlineClaimScope = that item's fileScope, and sessionTree = the resolved orchestrator tree (SG-9: entry.tree ?? workspace root — with the committed empty-tree default the absolute path would normalize to 'repo/src/a.ts' and match nothing, so this row fails without the fix). No second path matcher exists in continuation.ts; journaled gates/allow

the SAME orchestrator edit ask, differing ONLY in the claim, is replied REJECT with response 'reject' — asserted for three no-claim shapes: (a) no item carries an inlineClaim; (b) an item carries a claim but its fileScope does not cover the asked path; (c) the claim is on an item at PUBLISHED (SG-8: a claim on a finished item covers nothing). A fourth shape pins decideEdit's own guards reaching the ask path: an ask for a path containing a `..` segment, or under .conductor/, is REJECTED even when a claim scope would otherwise glob-match it (gates-edit.ts:169, :190). No claim, no edit — G8 survives

the active-claim scope is ONE exported derivation feeding BOTH gates. plugin/index.ts:238 hardcodes inlineClaimScope:null today, so a claimed edit would be denied by tool.execute.before before the permission ask was ever raised and the allow path above would be unreachable in production. Asserted end to end on one fixture: with the claim active, gateBeforeToolCall for the orchestrator's edit of that path does NOT throw AND the permission reply is 'once'; with the claim removed, gateBeforeToolCall throws the G8 reason AND the reply is 'reject'. Both seams read the same function — a fixture cannot exist where one allows and the other denies

SG-10 fail-closed: an orchestrator edit ask from whose payload no concrete file path can be extracted — metadata carries neither filePath nor path, and patterns is absent, empty, or wildcard-only — is REJECTED and journaled gates/deny naming the unextractable payload, EVEN WHEN an active claim exists. The wire contract pins only id/sessionID/permission (wire-notes.md:110), so an unrecognized payload shape must degrade to 'the claim does not work', never to 'the orchestrator may edit anything'

§3.5: an ORCHESTRATOR ask with permission 'question' is ALLOWED (response 'once') but counted and journaled with Task 1.5's verdict — one gates/allow record whose data carries permission:'question' and humanTerritory = core/decide.ts isHumanTerritory(question text). BOTH polarities asserted on real strings: a §6.2 question ('should we delete the production data before the migration?') journals true, a derivable technical question ('should the parser use a Map or a plain object?') journals false. When no question text can be extracted from the payload the record carries humanTerritory false plus an explicit textAvailable false — the verdict is never fabricated — and the reply is still allow

an orchestrator ask whose permission is neither 'edit' (claim-adjudicated) nor 'question' (allowed) — e.g. 'bash' or an unrecognized future kind — is REJECTED and journaled gates/deny naming the kind. The ask-gate's default is deny: a permission vocabulary that grows upstream must not silently widen what the orchestrator may do

the reply route failing — the client returning an envelope with an `error`, or throwing outright — is journaled once at error level and does NOT propagate out of the handler or the event hook; no state is written and no re-prompt is triggered by the failure. Asserted for both failure shapes through the extended fake. opencode's own permission timeout is then the backstop; conductor does not compound a transport failure with a crash (G5)

C-029(b) BINDING (SG-6, enforced inside handleDecide at adapter/tools.ts:740 beside the existing requireTwoOptions check at :757): a kind:'derived' decision whose `question` satisfies core/decide.ts isHumanTerritory is REJECTED BEFORE PERSIST — the call throws a reason naming §6.2 human territory, decisions.jsonl gains ZERO lines (byte-identical, and the next successful decide still mints the next sequential D-id), and the same question is SURFACED instead as a schema-valid §2.11 QuestionRecord via adapter/questions.ts appendQuestion with humanTerritory true, origin 'surface-tool' (the closed QUESTION_ORIGINS vocabulary is NOT widened) and blocksItems []. Two controls in the same row: the identical question with kind:'human' is ACCEPTED and appends its line as before, and a derived decision on a technical question is unaffected — the existing 9.1 tests for handleDecide keep passing unchanged

C-032 E7 BINDING, repair half: at idle, BEFORE any re-prompt or stop decision, the engine reconciles the half-applied blockAndAsk/blockVetAndAsk window (adapter/tools.ts:2797, :3262 append the question first and setBlocked second). Fixture: an OPEN question with origin 'implementer-blocked' whose blocksItems names an item whose blocked is null. The engine completes the write idempotently via store.setBlocked(runId, itemId, {reason naming the open question, stage, questionId}), journals state:item.updated, and appends NO new question. Controls: a fully-applied pair (question open, item blocked with a matching blocked.questionId) is left byte-identical — no second write — and an ANSWERED question never re-blocks anything. After reconciliation the item is answerable through the normal path, because answerQuestion clears exactly the items whose blocked.questionId matches

C-032 E7 BINDING, prevention half: blockAndAsk and blockVetAndAsk REUSE an already-open question for the same item instead of appending a second — before appending, each looks for an OPEN question (answeredIso null) with origin 'implementer-blocked' whose blocksItems contains this itemId, and when one exists it re-points the item's blocked at THAT question id rather than minting a new one. Asserted separately for each of the two call sites: two consecutive blocking calls on the same item leave EXACTLY ONE record in questions.jsonl and item.blocked.questionId naming it, while the item's accumulated attempts counters still increase on both calls (the accumulation the C-029 fix established is preserved). A blocking call for a DIFFERENT item still mints its own question

C-056 BINDING, the residual that ratification left open and that the 32 authored rows do not cover. handleSurface (adapter/tools.ts:897-914) records which named items are ALREADY blocked but appends its question anyway, so an item can be named by TWO open questions while item.blocked carries only the FIRST (first-block-wins, ratified at C-056). Answering the first therefore RELEASES the item while the second is still open and still names it. RULE: releasing an item on answer must re-block it on the OLDEST still-open question that names it, if any, and release only when none remains. Asserted in both directions on a real questions ledger: (a) I1 named by Q1 then Q2, answering Q1 leaves I1 blocked with blocked.questionId == Q2 and the item NOT schedulable; (b) answering Q2 then releases I1 with blocked null. The ordering half matters as much as the re-block: first-block-wins is only coherent if the successor is chosen oldest-first.
